answer: A haven lookout bond charges each identity for one comet passage. The claimant locks a 70-credit bond, registers one haven lookout, and files the comet passage time and its ember flash code from the ephemeris table. An auditor recomputes time and code from that table and the coordinates; a wrong time, reused code, or duplicate lookout burns the bond. The first filing costs 36, the kth 36+6(k-1), the 1000th 6030, so 1000 fakes pay 3,033,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-lookout ring fails when reused codes expose both claims. An honest lookout pays 36 once and reclaims the bond.
